sent_subject: Meta GEM launches today: a 3‑variant kidswear test to beat ad fatigue
sent:
Amrita —

Meta just rolled out its Generative Ads Model (GEM): one model now optimizes creative and placements across Facebook, Instagram, Reels and Stories. In Meta’s tests it delivered up to 18.9% more conversions and 12% higher CTR — but it only helps if you feed it distinct angles.

Here’s a one‑week test we’d run for Sprout & Stitch:

- Three angles (three ads, same budget, automatic placements on):
  1) Rain‑Ready — raincoat + layers; first frame is a puddle splash; 5–15s phone video or loop; headline “Dry kids, happy park.”
  2) Knee‑Proof — close‑ups of reinforced knees; before/after or scrape test; headline “Built for slides, not sit‑still.”
  3) Under £20 — price‑forward grid of 4 bestsellers; headline “Playproof picks under £20.”

- Each ad links to a matching landing page (one promise, one CTA). Even a simple section page works if the hero keeps the ad’s promise.

- Let it run 5–7 days. Retire any variant with three straight days of falling click‑through; swap in a fresh cut, not a fresh idea.

- Judge winners by add‑to‑bag and first‑order rate vs. your home baseline, not just CTR.

Two setup notes:
- Keep targeting simple and leave placements on automatic; the lift comes from creative diversity, not audience micromanagement.
- Ship variants in threes on a schedule; aim to have the next three ready before the current set tires.

If you want, we can sketch the three lightweight landing blocks those ads need.

Fieldwork Studio
